item.title: Down to the wire: The Tipline for 27 February 2026
item.description: Charter and Cox Enterprises have received regulatory approval for their $34.5 billion tie-up to create a cable and broadband giant. The Federal Communications Commission found no antitrust concerns, celebrating Charter’s promises to end its diversity hiring programmes, add jobs in the US and provide employees with “Invest in America” Trump accounts. “By approving this deal, the FCC ensures big win...

item.title: DOJ backs patent holders’ ability to seek injunction
item.description: Non-practising patent holders can demonstrate the need for a permanent injunction prohibiting future infringement, the Department of Justice has said, further cementing the Antitrust Division’s embrace of stronger intellectual property protections.

item.title: Five firms guide Paramount on blockbuster Warner Bros deal
item.description: Paramount utilised at least five law firms to help push for clearance of its $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros, as Democrats lined up behind state enforcers in hopes of blocking the deal.

item.title: The room where it happens: The Briefing for 2 March 2026
item.description: Marriott, Hilton and InterContinental may be pondering repeat-stay suites for their antitrust counsel after the UK’s Competition and Markets Authority revealed it is investigating whether the hotel chains unlawfully shared commercially sensitive information via CoStar’s pricing analytics tool. The probe comes just five months after the companies defeated a private antitrust lawsuit on the other si...

item.title: Economists take aim at CMA’s ‘ill-suited’ approach to dynamic efficiencies
item.description: Several leading economics consultancies are pushing for the UK’s Competition and Markets Authority to reform its current framework for assessing efficiencies during merger control reviews by better considering dynamic, long-term effects.

item.title: Oxera bolsters partnership with CMA hire
item.description: The UK’s Competition and Markets Authority has suffered the third departure of a senior economist in as many months, after Oxera poached one of its directors.

item.title: German government tight-lipped on potential Cosco national security probe
item.description: The majority acquisition of German logistics business Konrad Zippel Spediteur by the Chinese state-owned shipping company Cosco is expected to attract foreign investment scrutiny by ministers in Berlin.

item.title: In like a lion: The Tipline for 2 March 2026
item.description: Let’s hope the American Bar Association’s Spring Meeting badges have not already been printed. O’Melveny & Myers, Winston & Strawn, Clifford Chance and Apple have all recently revealed lateral hires. item.title: Live Nation trial to test DOJ’s jury strategy
item.description: The Department of Justice’s monopolisation suit against Live Nation may be the first civil case the Antitrust Division has ever tried before a jury, serving as a potential bellwether for future Section 2 cases.

item.title: DOJ rebukes information exchange defence
item.description: The Department of Justice has rebuffed claims made by producers of frozen potato products that reciprocal information exchanges are “insufficient” to establish concerted action.
